title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from p.772: X is a surface (Riemann surface or 2-manifold), S ⊂ X has x as an isolated point, U = X∖S, D_x^* is a punctured disc around x, and D_x^{*~} → D_x^* is a universal cover. T_x = Aut(D_x^{*~}/D_x^*) ≅ π_1(D_x^*) ≅ Z (the local monodromy or 'inertia' group). Since the covering category Rev(U) is multigalois (e.g. U locally 1-connected), the pullback functor Rev(U) → Rev(D_x^{*~}) composed with global sections, U' ↦ Γ(D_x^{*~}, U' ×_U D_x^{*~}), is a fibre functor. The fundamental group π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) is its automorphism group. This is a fundamental group with a 'base point' that is the universal cover of a punctured disc, rather than a point.

The homomorphism (60) K_x : T_x → π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) is described in two ways. First, as the map π_1(D_x^*, D_x^{*~}) → π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) induced by the inclusion D_x^* ⊂ U. Second, in fibre-functor terms: T_x acts on D_x^{*~} by deck transformations. Hence it acts on the fibre product U'_{D^{*~}} through the first factor (shown in the square diagram). Hence it acts on its set of sections, naturally in U'.

Comparison with a previously chosen fundamental group π = π_1(U, Ũ), Ũ a universal cover of U. Choose a 'class of paths' from D_x^{*~} to Ũ, i.e. an isomorphism (62) Ũ ≅ Revuniv(U, D_x^{*~}). Here Revuniv(U, D_x^{*~}) is the universal cover representing (pro-representing) the fibre functor. Such isomorphisms form a π-torsor.

The marginal NB describes a concrete choice. If D_x^{*~} is the universal cover of a smaller punctured disc D_{x,i}^* ⊂ D_x, then Revuniv(U, D_x^{*~}) ≅ Revuniv(U, D_{x,i}^{*~}), i.e. compatibility under shrinking the disc.

On the next page, (62) gives an isomorphism (63) π ≅ π_1(U, D_x^{*~}), well defined up to inner automorphism. Composing with (60) gives T_x → π, whose outer class is the outer homomorphism π_1(D_x^*) → π_1(U). This is the inertia/local monodromy class at the puncture x.

Purpose: setting up the topological prototype of inertia subgroups and 'tangential' base points for the Teichmüller/Galois tower analysis in La Longue Marche. The next section ties the choice of D_x^{*~} to germs of arcs.
errors: No mathematical error. The transcription's 'T_α' is surely T_x.
The action of T_x on sections should be read as transport of structure (s ↦ t∘s∘t^{-1}); the note leaves this implicit.

ideas.what: Fundamental group based at the universal cover of a punctured disc, defined as automorphisms of the fibre functor Rev(U) → Rev(D_x^{*~})
ideas.modern_name: tangential base point / base point at a puncture (topological version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); also Grothendieck's Esquisse/Longue Marche informally
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) uses such base points; Esquisse d'un programme mentions tangential base points

ideas.what: Canonical local monodromy homomorphism T_x → π_1(U, D_x^{*~}), and outer homomorphism π_1(D_x^*) → π_1(U) after a choice of path class
ideas.modern_name: inertia subgroup / local monodromy at a puncture, defined up to conjugacy

ideas.what: Path classes between fibre functors as isomorphisms of universal covers, forming a π-torsor
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid with fibre functors as objects (étale paths)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard construction: inertia homomorphisms via fibre functors at universal covers of punctured discs, i.e. tangential base points. This is well known from SGA1 and from Deligne's tangential base points, and Grothendieck already circulated it in La Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: The marginal NB reads roughly: 'NB si D_x^{*~} défini par un rev. universel D_{x,i}^{*~} d'un disque épointé D_{x,i}^* (⊂ D_x), et si ... ∈ Ũ, Revuniv(U, D_x^{*~}) ≃ Revuniv(U, D_{x,i}^{*~}) ...'. The label '(G?)' is the equation number (62).
